World Steel Association (worldsteel) (2026). Energy use in the steel industry. Web page, worldsteel.org, dated May 2026. https://worldsteel.org/about-steel/energy-use-in-the-steel-industry/ (accessed 2026-11-04).

background: Overview web page: route-level shares of energy inputs and a global energy-intensity trend; no technology-level energy per unit of product, cost, capacity or TRL. What it has: Global steelmaking energy intensity 20.95 GJ/t (2024), about 50 GJ/t in the 1960s; Table 1 energy input shares by route (BF-BOF coal 70-80%, electricity 10-15%, gas 5-15%; EAF 100% scrap 5-15/50-70/10-25%; EAF 70% DRI 5-15/25-40/40-60%); upstream raw material energy ~10% (BF-BOF) and ~5% (EAF) of total; co-product gases >60% of plant energy; 1.94% renewable energy (2024); 1,849.4 Mt crude steel in 2025. Successor to IISI (worldsteel's former name) energy-use publications such as IISI 1998, which is not held. Page dated "May 2026 | AP/RJ"; parsed from the text/html part of the mhtml.
